title: Homotopy Segal spaces, mapping fibers and homotopy-category isomorphisms
statement: Use simplicial sets, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalences and the path-model homotopy fibers of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A simplicial space is a functor $X:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$. For $r\geq2$, form the simplicial set $H_r(X)$ of $r$ edges $e_0,\ldots,e_{r-1}\in X_1$ and $r-1$ paths $p_j\in\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X_0)$ satisfying $\operatorname{ev}_0p_j=d_0e_j$ and $\operatorname{ev}_1p_j=d_1e_{j+1}$ in every inner degree, with coordinatewise operators. The canonical comparison $X_r\to H_r(X)$ takes the consecutive edges and constant paths at their common vertices. Define a homotopy Segal space by requiring every $X_n$ to be Kan and every such comparison to be a weak homotopy equivalence. For a list $\mathbf x=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ of vertices of $X_0$, set $T_X(\mathbf x)=\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathbf x}(X_n\to X_0^{n+1})$, using all the vertex inclusions. Write $M_X(x,y)=T_X(x,y)$; the finite power $X_0^2$ is the degreewise product $X_0\times X_0$ and the map is $(d_1,d_0)$. Restriction along a monotone simplex map restricts both a simplex and its entire vertex-list path. A map $F:X\to Y$ induces $M_X(x,y)\to M_Y(Fx,Fy)$ by applying $F_1$ to the edge and postcomposing the endpoint path with $F_0\times F_0$. The morphisms of $hX$ are $\pi_0M_X(x,y)$; the identity is the component of $s_0x$ with the constant endpoint path. Record composition by its graph: $[g]\circ[f]=[h]$ precisely when a component of $T_X(x,y,z)$ restricts under $d_2,d_0,d_1$ to $[f],[g],[h]$, respectively. For a homotopy Segal space this is the degree-two Segal composition, equivalently its graph, with associative unital laws from the degree-three simplicial identities and degeneracies. Define $x\cong y$ in $hX$ by the existence of $[f]\in\pi_0M_X(x,y)$ and $[g]\in\pi_0M_X(y,x)$ with $[g]\circ[f]=[\mathrm{id}_x]$ and $[f]\circ[g]=[\mathrm{id}_y]$. No inverse comparison or triangle is chosen as data.

from.place: Mapping-space foundation: the explicit homotopy-Segal comparisons, endpoint mapping fibers, and isomorphisms in their homotopy category used to state the DK diagonal criterion.

lean.note: Every construction has explicit data and structural proofs, with no postponed theorem or sorry. Composition and isomorphism are expressed by their canonical graph on components of triangle homotopy fibers, retaining the same morphisms and both inverse equations. The node owns the definitions introduced in the parent statement.
